## Access type 
- **ApiServer:** This access type indicates that a call used the Kubernetes API server. This could be a normal API resource request but also a call via kube-proxy.
- **DirectIp:** The internal IP address of the requested resource was used for the call. This can either be a pod or a node. This access type can only be applied if you run a containerized ActiveGate inside the Kubernetes cluster.

1.title: Top endpoints average queries per minute
1.description: List the top number of average API requests per minute to endpoints of monitored Kubernetes clusters.

4.title: Failing queries per minute
4.description: Shows the number of failed API requests per minute to endpoints of monitored Kubernetes clusters.
4.query: timeseries { sum(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_count, rate: 1m), value.A = avg(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_count, rate: 1m, scalar: true) }, by: { k8s.cluster.name }, filter: { NOT matchesValue(status_code, "2*") AND ( matchesValue(k8s.cluster.name, $Cluster) AND matchesValue(dt.active_gate.id, $ActiveGateId) ) }

5.title: Successful queries per minute
5.description: Shows the number of successful API requests per minute to endpoints of monitored Kubernetes clusters in the last 2 hours.
5.query: timeseries { sum(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_count, rate: 1m), value.A = avg(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_count, rate: 1m, scalar: true) }, by: { k8s.cluster.name }, filter: { matchesValue(status_code, "2*") AND matchesValue(k8s.cluster.name, $Cluster) AND matchesValue(dt.active_gate.id, $ActiveGateId) }

6.title: Average latency successful queries
6.description: Shows the average latency of successful API requests to endpoints of monitored Kubernetes clusters.
6.query: timeseries { avg(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_duration, rate: 1m), value.A = avg(dt.sfm.active_gate.kubernetes.api.query_duration, rate: 1m, scalar: true) }, by: { k8s.cluster.name }, filter: { matchesValue(status_code, "2*") AND matchesValue(k8s.cluster.name, $Cluster) AND matchesValue(dt.active_gate.id, $ActiveGateId) }

8.title: Failing queries
8.description: List the top number of failed API requests to endpoints of monitored Kubernetes clusters.

10.title: Cluster Monitoring Availability
10.description: Displays the availability of Cluster Monitoring
10.query:
timeseries
  data = min(dt.kubernetes.cluster.readyz),
  by: {k8s.cluster.name},
  interval: 1m,
  shift: -2m
| filter in(k8s.cluster.name, $Cluster)
| fieldsAdd sumDataPoints = arraySum(data), numDataPoints = arraySize(data)
| fields `Kubernetes cluster` = k8s.cluster.name, `Availability (%)` = (sumDataPoints / numDataPoints) * 100

11.content:
## Status codes
The following list gives you some hints for investigation based on the most common status codes.

* **-1: General error.** Dynatrace could not access the endpoint. See \"Status reasons\" for more details. **Prometheus:** The [pod annotations](https://dt-url.net/y942vsf#annotate-prometheus-exporter-pods) might be incorrect.

* **401: Unauthorized.** If you connect via URL and token, please double-check that the values are correct.

- **403: Forbidden.** The service account might lack [required permissions](https://dt-url.net/un02v1h).

* **404: Not Found.** The resource does not exist. This can happen when resources were deleted. **Prometheus:** It is likely that the [`metrics.dynatrace.com/path`](https://dt-url.net/y942vsf#path-to-metrics-endpoint) annotation points to a non-existent endpoint.

* **503: Service Unavailable.** The Kubernetes API experiences an outage. **Prometheus:** The [`metrics.dynatrace.com/port`](https://dt-url.net/y942vsf#metrics-port) annotation might contain a wrong value. Another common reason for this status code are wrong TLS settings.

14.content:
## Status reasons
The following list gives you some hints for investigation based on the most common status codes.


- **HttpStatus:** The status code represents an HTTP status code. See \"Status codes\" for more details.

- **ConnectionError:** Signals that an error occurred while attempting to connect a socket to a remote address and port. Typically, the connection was refused remotely (e.g., no process is listening on the remote address/port).

- **NoRouteToHost:** Signals that an error occurred while attempting to connect a socket to a remote address and port. Typically, the remote host cannot be reached because of an intervening firewall, or if an intermediate router is down.

- **SocketTimeout:** Signals that a timeout has occurred on a socket read or accept.

- **ConnectionTimeout:** A timeout occurred while connecting to an HTTP server.

- **SslError:** Indicates an error detected by an SSL subsystem. This class is the general class of exceptions produced by failed SSL-related operations.

- **InvalidContentType:** The response content type does not match the expected content type. Please check the logs for more info.

15.title: Clusters with unhealthy ActiveGates
15.description:
**Query Explanation:**  
This query identifies Kubernetes clusters with API monitoring enabled and linked to specific ActiveGates. It evaluates ActiveGate health metrics (CPU usage, memory usage, and garbage collection time) over the last 30 minutes. Based on thresholds, it flags unhealthy ActiveGates and lists the conditions causing the issues (e.g., high CPU or memory usage).  

**Why this visualization is useful:**  
The table provides a clear overview of clusters and their associated ActiveGates, highlighting problematic conditions. This helps quickly identify clusters impacted by resource constraints or performance issues, enabling targeted troubleshooting.

17.content:
### Conditions explanation

The DQL query thresholds for unhealthy conditions are based on the [Sizing guide for Dynatrace ActiveGates in the Kubernetes monitoring use-case](https://dt-url.net/26agsizes#monitoring-and-validation).

#### High CPU usage

- The ActiveGate's JVM CPU usage exceeded 85% for more than three samples within the last 30 minutes.

#### High memory usage

- The ActiveGate's JVM memory usage (used / available memory) exceeded 80% for more than three samples within the last 30 minutes.
- The ActiveGate's JVM garbace collection time exceeded 3 seconds for more than three samples within the last 30 minutes.

18.title: ActiveGate JVM CPU usage
18.description:
**Description:**  
This tile displays the maximum CPU usage of ActiveGates over time.

**Purpose:**
The line chart visualization highlights trends and fluctuations, enabling quick identification of performance spikes or resource bottlenecks.

19.title: ActiveGate JVM memory usage
19.description:
**Description:**  
This tile visualizes the percentage of heap memory used by ActiveGates over time, calculated as `memory_used / memory_available * 100`.

**Purpose:**
The line chart effectively highlights trends and fluctuations in memory usage, enabling proactive monitoring and capacity planning.

20.title: ActiveGate JVM garbage collection time
20.description:
**Description:**  
This tile displays the maximum major garbage collection time for ActiveGates 

**Purpose:**  
The line chart helps visualize trends and fluctuations in garbage collection times, enabling quick identification of performance bottlenecks or anomalies in ActiveGate JVMs.
